g.text: CHAPTER I • THE TANDOOR & SIGRI
Folio 01
MENUQR ROYAL ARCHIVES • ESTD 1924
THE ART OF GALOUTI
शाही गलौटी व तंदूरी कबाब
Galouti Kebab Nawabi
Young pasture mutton pounded 4 times into an ethereal silk purée, infused with 160 secret
botanical herbs, and smoked over burning cloves and aged cow ghee. Melts on the tongue.
Served with Ulte Tawe Ka Saffron Paratha, Pickled Shallots & Mint Chutney
Bhatti Murgh Angara
Boneless chicken thigh steeped 24 hours in pungent yellow mustard oil, Mathania chillies,
and hung yoghurt, roasted over glowing mariposa wood charcoal to blistered tenderness.
Kakori Seekh Royale
The aristocrat of kebabs: tenderized with raw papaya milk, cardamom powder, and rose petals,
threaded delicately on silver skewers and roasted over slow embers.
THE KHANSAMA'S BOTANICAL HERBARIUM
Chakra Phool • Star Anise
Selected 8-pointed seed pods conferring intoxicating sweet licorice and wood aroma.
Pampore Zaffran • Crimson Saffron
Grade-A Mongra stigmas from Kashmir valley, steeped in lukewarm milk to release floral gold.
Pathar Ke Phool • Black Stone Flower
Rare wild lichen harvested from deep forest rocks; gives authentic Awadhi kebabs their earthy soul.
VEGETARIAN SHAHI DASTARKHWAN
Folio 02
MENUQR ROYAL ARCHIVES • ESTD 1924
ROYAL VEGETARIAN DELICACIES
शाही पनीर पसंदा व नज़ाकत
Royal Paneer Pasanda
Twin triangular fillets of fresh Malai Paneer stuffed with golden sultanas, pistachios and khoya,
pan-seared in cow ghee, enveloped in a rich satin brown onion, cashew, and saffron velouté.
Garnished with 24K edible gold leaf, fresh ginger matchsticks & pomegranate reduction
Awadhi Dahi Ke Kebab
Silk hung curd folded with roasted gram flour, finely minced mint, green cardamom and crushed black pepper,
crisped golden in cow ghee to yield a molten cream core that dissolves upon touch.
Tandoori Malai Broccoli
Tender broccoli crowns steeped in cardamom cream, processed cheddar, roasted cashew cream,
and white pepper, char-grilled over acacia wood coals for subtle smokiness.
THE LAW OF THE COAL
"No gas flame can replicate what centuries of slow
charcoal embers whisper into meat, cream, and curd."
— Ustad Mir Baqir Ali, Chief Khansama to the Court of Awadh, 1924
TEMPERED IN CLAY OVEN AT 320°C
